items.title: Shortest path on a grid (BFS)
items.prompt: Order the lines so `shortest(grid, start, goal)` returns the number of steps between two cells of a grid of `'.'` (open) and `'#'` (wall), or -1 if unreachable.
lines: if 0 <= nr < len(grid) and 0 <= nc < len(grid[0]) and grid[nr][nc] == "." and (nr, nc) not in seen:
items.lesson: BFS explores in distance order, so the first time you pop the goal you have the shortest path. Mark cells as seen when you enqueue them (not when you pop) so no cell is queued twice.

items.title: LRU cache with OrderedDict
items.prompt: Order the lines to build an LRU cache: `get` returns -1 on a miss and refreshes recency on a hit; `put` evicts the least recently used key when over capacity.
lines: def __init__(self, cap): self.cap, self.d = cap, OrderedDict()
if k not in self.d: return -1
items.tests:
def test_miss():
    assert LRU(2).get("x") == -1

def test_get_refreshes():
    c = LRU(2); c.put("a", 1); c.put("b", 2)
    assert c.get("a") == 1
    c.put("c", 3)
    assert c.get("b") == -1, "b was least recently used"
    assert c.get("a") == 1 and c.get("c") == 3

def test_update_existing():
    c = LRU(1); c.put("a", 1); c.put("a", 5)
    assert c.get("a") == 5
items.lesson: Check the miss before touching the dict, then move_to_end on a hit so recency is updated before you return. popitem(last=False) removes the oldest entry.

items.title: Token bucket refill
items.prompt: Order the lines so `allow()` refills tokens based on elapsed time (capped at capacity) and then spends one if available. The clock is injected.
lines: self.rate, self.cap, self.clock, self.tokens, self.last = rate, capacity, clock, capacity, clock()
items.tests:
class Clock:
    t = 0.0
    def __call__(self):
        return self.t

def test_burst_then_block():
    clk = Clock(); b = TokenBucket(1, 2, clk)
    assert [b.allow(), b.allow(), b.allow()] == [True, True, False]

def test_refill():
    clk = Clock(); b = TokenBucket(2, 2, clk)
    b.allow(); b.allow()
    clk.t = 0.5
    assert b.allow() is True, "0.5 s at 2 tokens/s refills one token"
    assert b.allow() is False

def test_cap():
    clk = Clock(); b = TokenBucket(1, 2, clk)
    clk.t = 100
    assert sum(b.allow() for _ in range(5)) == 2, "refill is capped at capacity"
items.lesson: Refill first (using time since the last refill, capped at capacity), update `last`, and only then decide. Updating `last` before computing elapsed time would refill nothing.

items.title: Agent tool-use loop
items.prompt: Order the lines so `run(client, messages, tools)` keeps calling the model, runs each requested tool, sends the results back in a user turn, and returns the final text.
lines: calls = [b for b in resp["content"] if b["type"] == "tool_use"]
results = [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": b["id"], "content": tools[b["name"]](**b["input"])} for b in calls]
items.lesson: Append the assistant turn before checking stop_reason so the history is complete; only a "tool_use" stop continues the loop, and the tool results must go in the next user turn, each tagged with its tool_use_id.

items.title: Retry with exponential backoff
items.prompt: Order the lines so `retry(fn, sleep)` retries transient errors with delays 1, 2, 4, ... and re-raises after the last attempt. `sleep` is injected.
items.lesson: `return fn()` sits inside try so success exits immediately; the last-attempt check comes before sleeping so you re-raise without a pointless final wait. Injecting `sleep` keeps tests instant.

items.title: Binary search (leftmost index)
items.prompt: Order the lines so `lower_bound(xs, t)` returns the first index i with xs[i] >= t in a sorted list.
items.lesson: Use a half-open range [lo, hi) with `while lo < hi`; move lo past mid when xs[mid] is too small, otherwise keep mid as a candidate (hi = mid). This always terminates and returns the insertion point.

items.title: Longest substring without repeats
items.prompt: Order the lines so `longest_unique(s)` returns the length of the longest substring with no repeated characters.
lines: if ch in last and last[ch] >= left:
items.lesson: Shrink the window (move left past the previous occurrence) before recording the new position and measuring; otherwise the window still contains the duplicate.

items.title: Merge overlapping intervals
items.prompt: Order the lines so `merge(intervals)` merges overlapping [start, end] pairs.
items.lesson: Sort by start first; then each interval either extends the last merged one (take the max end, since it may be contained) or starts a new one.

items.title: Topological sort (Kahn's algorithm)
items.prompt: Order the lines so `topo(deps)` returns an order where every task comes after its dependencies; `deps` maps task -> list of tasks it depends on. Raise ValueError on a cycle.
lines: indeg = {t: len(d) for t, d in deps.items()}
ready, order = [t for t, n in indeg.items() if n == 0], []
for u in [u for u, d in deps.items() if t in d]:
items.lesson: Start from tasks with no unmet dependencies; when one finishes, decrement its dependents and release those that hit zero. If some tasks never reach zero, there is a cycle.

items.title: Safe JSON parse of model output
items.prompt: Order the lines so `parse(text, required)` strips a ```json fence, parses, validates that the result is an object with the required keys, and returns None on any failure.
lines: return None  # not JSON at all
if not isinstance(data, dict) or any(k not in data for k in required):
items.lesson: Clean the text before parsing, keep only json.loads inside the try (so you don't hide other bugs), and validate shape after parsing: valid JSON is not the same as the JSON you asked for.

items.title: Assemble a streamed response
items.prompt: Order the lines so `assemble(events)` rebuilds the text of each content block from streaming events (`content_block_start`, `content_block_delta`, `message_delta`) and returns `(texts, stop_reason)`.
lines: return [blocks[i] for i in sorted(blocks)], stop
items.tests:
EVENTS = [
    {"type": "message_start"},
    {"type": "content_block_start", "index": 0},
    {"type": "content_block_delta", "index": 0, "delta": {"text": "Hel"}},
    {"type": "content_block_start", "index": 1},
    {"type": "content_block_delta", "index": 1, "delta": {"text": "B"}},
    {"type": "content_block_delta", "index": 0, "delta": {"text": "lo"}},
    {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": 0},
    {"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "end_turn"}},
    {"type": "message_stop"},
]

def test_assemble():
    assert assemble(EVENTS) == (["Hello", "B"], "end_turn")

def test_empty_stream():
    assert assemble([]) == ([], None)
items.lesson: Key deltas by block index (blocks can interleave), create the block on content_block_start before appending deltas, and read stop_reason from message_delta, which arrives at the end.

items.title: Top-k most common words
items.prompt: Order the lines so `top_words(text, k)` returns the k most common lower-cased words as (word, count) pairs.
items.lesson: Normalise (lower-case, tokenise) before counting, otherwise 'The' and 'the' are different keys. Counter.most_common(k) does the sort for you (ties keep first-seen order).

items.title: Dataclass with default_factory
items.prompt: Order the lines to define a `Conversation` dataclass whose `messages` list is fresh per instance, with an `add(role, text)` method that returns self for chaining.
items.tests:
def test_independent_lists():
    a, b = Conversation(), Conversation()
    a.add("user", "hi")
    assert b.messages == [], "each instance needs its own list"

def test_chain():
    c = Conversation(model="x").add("user", "a").add("assistant", "b")
    assert [m["role"] for m in c.messages] == ["user", "assistant"] and c.model == "x"
items.lesson: @dataclass must sit directly above the class, and mutable defaults need field(default_factory=list); a bare `= []` is rejected because it would be shared by every instance.

items.title: Bounded concurrent requests
items.prompt: Order the lines so `fetch_all(fetch, items, limit)` runs `fetch` concurrently, never more than `limit` at once, and returns results in input order.
lines: return await asyncio.gather(*(one(x) for x in items))
items.tests:
import asyncio

async def test_order_and_limit():
    live, peak = 0, 0
    async def fetch(x):
        nonlocal live, peak
        live += 1; peak = max(peak, live)
        await asyncio.sleep(0.001 * (5 - x))
        live -= 1
        return x * 10
    out = await fetch_all(fetch, [1, 2, 3, 4], 2)
    assert out == [10, 20, 30, 40], "gather keeps input order"
    assert peak <= 2, f"peak concurrency {peak} > limit"
    assert peak == 2, "should actually run in parallel"
items.lesson: Create the semaphore once, outside the per-item coroutine, so all tasks share it; acquire it around the awaited call; then gather (and await) all coroutines, which preserves input order.

items.title: Timing context manager
items.prompt: Order the lines so `timed(name, log, clock)` records `(name, elapsed)` in `log` when the block exits, even if it raised.
items.lesson: Read the start time before yielding; the `yield` is where the with-block runs, and putting it in try/finally guarantees the exit code runs on exceptions too.

items.title: Pair with target sum (two pointers)
items.prompt: Order the lines so `pair_sum(xs, target)` returns a pair of values from the sorted list `xs` that add up to `target`, or None.
items.lesson: Start the pointers at both ends of the sorted list; a sum that is too small can only grow by moving the left pointer right, and a sum too big only shrinks by moving the right one left.
